shellWords.strategy: Adapt quote-aware literal/basic variable/positional/PIPESTATUS fields, IFS rules, scalar contexts and command-name promotion into the original streaming engine. Structural protection replaces sentinel strings. Declaration syntax requires an unquoted literal command and assignment prefix; retained raw spelling rejects escapes lost by token decoding, using only continuation removal from normalize_raw_word. An original bounded engine adapter uses the unchanged public Lexer raw-capture API for top-level declaration words not retained by the parser; quoted-at words trim leading mixed-IFS delimiters as verified with GNU Bash, diverging from upstream where needed. Cooperative Budget work, intermediate byte/element bounds and aggregate command field/byte limits reject overflow instead of truncating. No parser modifications, general parameter operators, globbing, substitutions, mapfile or output buffering are ported.

shellParameterDefaults.strategy: Adapt only ordinary scalar ${v-word}, ${v:-word}, ${v+word} and ${v:+word}. Preserve unset versus empty and select operands lazily without copying unused values. A cooperative engine scanner streams quote-protected operand pieces into existing Fields; the engine injects no quote sentinels. Single quotes protect unquoted operands and remain literal inside outer double quotes. Reparse only admitted basic-variable or scalar +/- tokens through the unchanged parser API, with at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes per synchronous call and 32 scalar-operator levels. The lexer retains raw operand backslashes in outer double quotes, and nested ${...} remains structural inside literal apostrophe spans. Parser operand and quoted-word boundary scans keep raw escapes and existing lexer protection indivisible. The engine scanner removes escapes once, uses quote context for literal process-substitution lookalikes, and recognizes opaque substitution boundaries without evaluating them; heredoc/comment syntax in those skipped regions fails closed. Simple-command redirects and argv share Work. Cumulative token bytes and eight reserved work steps per parsed byte share the command Work allowance with scanning and expansion; all admission loops yield and check cancellation. Check parsed shape instead of accepting parser literal fallbacks. Large literal operands bypass reparsing and retain existing intermediate/aggregate expansion and argument limits. Tests adapt unset cases by leaving variables absent, observe argv directly, and add lazy nested unsupported operands, quotes, IFS, scalar contexts, budgets, depth, size and cancellation regressions. The existing WASI runner explicitly includes words.rs. Assignment/error operators, arrays/list operands, indirection, pattern operations, globbing, tilde, brace expansion, arithmetic and substitutions remain unsupported when selected. Independent regressions cover escaped dollars, braced variables, quoted process-substitution lookalikes and escaped backticks, including nested, scalar and IFS contexts. Parser changes are recorded under shellParser.changeLog; upstream tests, captured oracle, baseline, mapfile implementation and output buffering remain unchanged.
